title: OpenAI refers Darren Zhou's ChatGPT plans to rape and kill his ex-girlfriend to the FBI; Palm Beach County deputies book him on 29 May 2026, six days after the alert, and he pleads guilty to stalking and threat charges
summary: OpenAI flagged a Florida man's ChatGPT plans to kill his ex to the FBI; PBSO booked him 29 May 2026, six days later; guilty plea 13 Aug
account: Darren Zhou, 25, a Goldman Sachs analyst from South Palm Beach, wrote to ChatGPT between March and May 2026 that he would rape and kill his 21-year-old ex-girlfriend and her family, claiming to own an AR-15. OpenAI's reviewers reported the conversations to the FBI, which passed two months of his messages to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office on 23 May 2026. Deputies matched the chats to anonymous threatening texts she had kept but not reported and booked him on 29 May. On 13 August 2026 he pleaded guilty to written threats to kill, aggravated stalking and misuse of a two-way device; adjudication withheld, with eight years' probation, two on a GPS monitor, a firearm ban and a no-contact order.
purpose: OpenAI says that when it detects users planning to harm others it routes the conversations to a small team trained on its usage policies and that, if human reviewers find an imminent threat of serious physical harm to others, it may refer the case to law enforcement; this referral is that designed use. ChatGPT itself is a general-purpose assistant, which Zhou used to rehearse his plans.
system: ChatGPT (OpenAI), with OpenAI's automated detection and human review pipeline for users planning to harm others
domain: Public safety - stalking and threat investigation
segment: Consumer chatbot trust-and-safety referral to law enforcement
taxonomy_note: A protective police intervention is not among the six types; chosen, as for the database's Meta-to-police alert record, because the documented gain is routing a platform alert into a sheriff's investigation and arrest within six days. Improved Knowledge Discovery was the alternative: the victim had not reported the threats, so without the referral police had no case. protective response with prevention unproven rather than specific harm prevented because no attack had begun, the plea was to stalking and threat offenses with adjudication withheld, and his lawyer says he owned no firearms. The PBSO booking blotter records his booking at 15:21 on 29 May 2026 and release on 30 May, six days after the FBI alert that WPBF dates to 23 May, matching the Sun Sentinel's interval. WPBF reports five years' probation where the Sun Sentinel, BocaNewsNow, IBTimes and MediaNama report eight.

ratings.reason: An anonymous campaign of rape and death threats that the 21-year-old had kept but not reported ended with his arrest, and the sentence bars contact and firearms for eight years with two on a GPS monitor; the affidavit found a credible threat and the State Attorney's Office says she approved the plea. No attack had begun, his lawyer says he owned no firearms and prosecutors accepted probation, so -4 is not established.

ai_role.statement: OpenAI's detection flagged the account and its human reviewers judged the threat serious enough for an emergency disclosure to the FBI; the records contained only Zhou's messages, not the chatbot's replies, and no source reports what ChatGPT answered him. Everything after was human: the FBI alerted PBSO on 23 May 2026, deputies did a welfare check, matched the chats to anonymous texts the victim had preserved, found a credible threat and booked him on 29 May; an assistant state attorney charged him in June and he pleaded guilty in August. A deputy who reviewed the material said it showed rehearsal and planning rather than venting.

produced_by: About two months of ChatGPT messages (March to May 2026) stating dated plans to kill a named ex-girlfriend, with her routine and claimed weapons, which OpenAI's pipeline flagged and its reviewers judged an imminent, credible threat
An OpenAI emergency disclosure to the FBI, passed to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office on 23 May 2026 with about two months of his messages
A PBSO investigation that corroborated the chats against anonymous threatening texts the victim had preserved, establishing probable cause for stalking and threat charges
must_hold: The user states the plan in the chat in enough detail for reviewers to judge it imminent and credible; OpenAI says it does not refer self-harm cases
The referral reaches a local agency able to act; here six days passed between the FBI's alert to PBSO and the booking
Independent corroboration exists: the victim had preserved the anonymous texts but had not reported them, so without the referral police had no case
The counterfactual is not established: no attack had begun, he pleaded to stalking and threat offenses with adjudication withheld, and his lawyer says he owned no firearms
